  • India's refineries operating at 105% to 108% of capacity, MRPL official says

    Over the last six months, Indian refiners have been running at above 100% capacity, driven by soaring diesel demand that leads them to focus more on this fuel compared to jet fuel. Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals intends to keep this high output rate through March. The ongoing Russia-Ukraine war has prompted refiners to diversify their crude oil sourcing, enabling a more adaptable production of diesel and jet fuel.

    Cognizant’s US green-card filings suspended amid fraud probe: What it means for employees

    Cognizant’s US green-card labour certification filings have been suspended amid a federal fraud investigation, according to Labor Department Inspector General Anthony D’Esposito. The move could delay some employees’ green-card sponsorship, but officials have not disclosed the allegations, number of affected cases or duration of the suspension.

    Tata Chemicals sets up high-level committee to decide on Kenya operations

    Tata Chemicals will establish a technical committee with Kenya to review regulatory issues. This committee will jointly be led by Kenyan mining officials and the subsidiary's CEO. The group will review concerns raised by the Ministry of Mining and submit a report. This development follows a recent "fruitful engagement" between officials and company executives. The committee aims to create a sustainable framework for responsible mining practices.

    Reliance Jio, Apple launch new RCS pricing for businesses in India, challenging WhatsApp

    Reliance Jio has introduced new pricing for business messaging services on iPhones. Apple has formally entered India's business messaging market, challenging WhatsApp's position. Businesses will pay new rates for marketing, transactional, and OTP messages starting September 1. Rival operators Vodafone Idea and Bharti Airtel are expected to join the Apple RCS ecosystem soon. This move accelerates RCS adoption in India, a leading market for the service.

    Dutch fintech Adyen sees long-term India opportunity, plans local expansion

    With plans for a substantial expansion in India's digital payments sector, Adyen is actively recruiting more staff to address surging demand. This growth is largely attributed to a rise in cross-border transactions and the influx of multinational clients. Since acquiring relevant licenses, Adyen has been enhancing its presence in India and now sees promising long-term growth opportunities ahead.

    Real estate sector needs policy reforms on affordability, approvals to unlock growth: Experts

    Rising land prices make affordable housing a significant challenge for common buyers. Streamlining processes and adopting technology are needed to improve ease of doing business. The sector is shifting towards constructing smarter and more sustainable buildings. Policy interventions are essential to support the sector's future growth.

    Tylenol use in pregnancy may be linked with uterus, ovary changes in daughters

    A recent study suggests Tylenol use by mothers during pregnancy may affect infant reproductive organ development. Researchers observed smaller ovaries and uteruses in three-month-old girls exposed to the drug. This exposure was also linked to fewer ovarian follicles and lower reproductive hormone levels. Long-term follow-up is needed to determine implications for future fertility and menopause timing. Current guidelines still recommend Tylenol as safe for pregnancy pain and fever relief.

Foreign investors have sold Indian government bonds since August. Global yields have risen significantly, impacting investment decisions. Bloomberg's decision to defer local debt inclusion also affected flows. Higher yields in developed markets narrowed the differential with Indian rates. Market participants anticipate largely neutral flows in the near future.

Cognizant’s US green-card filings suspended amid fraud probe: What it means for employees

Cognizant’s US green-card labour certification filings have been suspended amid a federal fraud investigation, according to Labor Department Inspector General Anthony D’Esposito. The move could delay some employees’ green-card sponsorship, but officials have not disclosed the allegations, number of affected cases or duration of the suspension.

French leaders react sharply to 'gender bias' at BAPS Eiffel Tower trip

French politicians and ministers have condemned allegations of gender discrimination during a private BAPS delegation visit to Paris’s Eiffel Tower. Staff alleged female employees were sidelined and replaced by men, prompting protests and an investigation. BAPS apologised for concerns raised, while India’s MEA called the matter an issue between concerned entities.

Air India's London-bound flight lands in Zurich amidst Heathrow's air traffic control issue

Air India flight AI 131 from Mumbai to London landed in Zurich after air traffic control-related problems at London Heathrow Airport. More than 290 passengers are onboard the aircraft and have been instructed to remain inside while awaiting further updates, with the situation at Heathrow expected to be resolved shortly.

India’s higher education moment has arrived just as the world turns inward

India’s universities are gaining global visibility just as studying abroad becomes costlier and more uncertain. Better rankings, tighter visa rules and foreign universities opening India campuses are changing the calculation for students: increasingly, the global education journey may begin at home.
